title: Work Zones, Equipment & Snowplows
citation: NJTR-1 Crash Report Manual (2023), Appendix: General Questions
key_points: A work zone runs from the first warning sign or device to the END ROAD WORK sign or last control device.
Complete an NJTR-1 when the traveling public (drivers, cyclists, pedestrians) is involved in a crash in, entering or leaving a work zone.
Crashes involving only workers, work vehicles and equipment inside the zone are work or OSHA incidents, not NJTR-1s.

faq.q: Does a work zone crash go on an NJTR-1?
faq.a: Yes, if the first harmful event happens inside the work zone or on the approach or exit, and it involves the traveling public. The data is used to judge how safe work-zone traffic plans are.

faq.q: Two pieces of work equipment collide inside the work zone.
faq.a: Not an NJTR-1. If everyone involved was part of the work activity, it's a work zone or OSHA incident.

faq.q: A forklift hits a pedestrian. Is that a crash?
faq.a: Inside a work zone with another worker, it's a work incident. It's an NJTR-1 if the forklift leaves the zone and hits a member of the public, or a member of the public enters the zone and hits a worker or equipment.

faq.q: A backhoe driving on the road runs off and hits a tree.
faq.a: Not reportable; a backhoe isn't built to carry passengers. If it collides with a driver or pedestrian who isn't part of the work zone, complete an NJTR-1.

faq.q: A snowplow actively plowing hits a parked car or fixed object.
faq.a: A crash report is appropriate because of the damage to the other vehicle. Fill in the plow's information like any other vehicle.

faq.q: A plow throws ice and snow onto a moving car.

faq.a: No. A pickup, dump truck or garbage truck with a plow is a vehicle in transport, and is only treated as a snowplow while the blade is down and it's actively clearing the road.
